newsitem.title: USA: Mass. high court - Delahunt wins disputed primary.
newsitem.headline: Mass. high court - Delahunt wins disputed primary.

text.p: In a one-line ruling Tuesday, the state's highest court declared Norfolk County, Mass., District Attorney William Delahunt the winner of the Democratic primary for the 10th congressional district.

"The judgment of the Superior Court is affirmed," the Supreme Judicial Court said. The lower court had ruled that Delahunt won the hotly-contested Democratic nomination for the seat being vacated by retiring 12-term Democrat Gerry Studds by 108 votes.

Delahunt turned to the courts after his opponent, Philip Johnston, who was first declared the winner and then continued to hold that position after recounts in selected district confirmed his lead by 175 votes.

Johnston was campaigning with first lady Hillary Clinton even as a Superior Court judge ruled late Friday that some 956 punchcard ballots had been miscounted and gave the Democratic slot for the Nov. 5 election to Delahunt.
Johnston filed suit with Massachusetts' highest court Monday asking five of the nine justices to recount the ballots on their own and declare him the winner.
Neither Johnston nor Delahunt was immediately available for comment.

The Republican nominee, Edward Teague, who has continued campaigning throughout the district that encompasses Cape Cod and the south shore of Massachusetts, has said it made little difference as to whom he faced in November.
"There's no difference between these candidates in terms of their opinions on critical issues," Teague said.
